meta.title: OAuth2 authorization-code login
meta.intro: How a web app signs a user in through an identity provider with the authorization-code flow. Pick a scenario and press **Next step →**.
meta.source: Generic example based on RFC 6749 and RFC 7636 (PKCE).

nodes.title: Browser
facts: Holds the user's IdP cookie and follows every **302**.
Never sees the client secret or the tokens.

nodes.title: Web app
facts: Creates `state` and the PKCE verifier, then exchanges the code on the back channel.

nodes.title: Authorize endpoint
facts: Authenticates the user and asks for consent.

nodes.title: Token endpoint
facts: Swaps a one-time code for tokens. Needs the client secret and the PKCE verifier.

nodes.title: Userinfo endpoint
facts: Returns the profile for a valid access token.

nodes.title: Session store
facts: Maps the session cookie to the user and refresh token.

scenarios.title: Successful sign-in
scenarios.lead: The user clicks **Sign in**, authenticates at the IdP and returns with a one-time code that the app trades for tokens.

steps.title: User opens /login
steps.what: The browser asks the app to start a login.
steps.fail: App down: the user sees a 502 and nothing has started.

steps.title: App redirects to the IdP
steps.what: A redirect carrying `client_id`, `state` and the PKCE `code_challenge`.
steps.where: `state` and the verifier are saved in the session.

steps.title: User signs in and consents
steps.what: The user types a password and approves the scopes.
steps.where: Only at the IdP. The app never sees the password.
steps.fail: Wrong password: the IdP re-prompts, the app is not involved.

steps.title: IdP returns a code
steps.where: Query string, valid for about 60 seconds.
steps.fail: `state` mismatch: the app rejects the callback (CSRF guard).

steps.title: App exchanges the code
steps.what: A back-channel POST with the code, secret and `code_verifier`.
steps.where: Server to server, never through the browser.
steps.fail: Expired or reused code: `invalid_grant`, the user must restart.

steps.title: App stores the session
steps.what: The app reads the profile and saves a session.
steps.fail: Redis down: login fails closed with a 503.

scenarios.title: User denies consent
scenarios.lead: The user clicks **Cancel** on the consent screen; the IdP sends an error back and the app shows a friendly message.

steps.title: App redirects to the IdP
steps.what: The same authorize redirect as the happy path.

steps.title: User declines
steps.what: The user refuses the requested scopes.
steps.fail: None: this is the user's choice.

steps.title: IdP returns an error
steps.what: A redirect with `error=access_denied` and the original `state`.
steps.fail: The app must check `state` before trusting `error`.

points: The browser carries only a **code**, never a token.
`state` stops forged callbacks; PKCE stops stolen codes.
Tokens stay in the **session store** behind an HttpOnly cookie.
